title: 2021 Quest Calendar - Monthly Recap - January
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K1YD12TDxwo

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a year-long experiment: the 2021 Quest Calendar, *The Dragon Staff of Maladoria*, an "adventure a day" desk calendar that swaps the usual daily comic or cute kitten for a few minutes of choose-your-path gamebook play. His plan is to recap each month as it ends, and this is January.

The setup is a mystery in the capital of Westhaven: the court wizard and his apprentice have vanished, a corrupting slime is spreading through the city, rats in the sewers are mutating, and the church has closed its doors. The first fortnight is a tutorial led by Godwin the Great, a half-elf wizard, covering stat checks, single-roll d20 combat resolved against a chart, and one-page dungeon maps where you trace a route through numbered chambers. Daniel then picks a half-elf druid from a roster that each credits its own artist, and the real adventure begins with rats, a poison trap in a sewer grate and a descent into the sewers.

He's candid about the pace: it took a month to learn the rules, pick a hero and fight some rats. He also defends it against complaints that it's slow. It's a calendar, after all, and a five-minute ritual before work has turned out to be comforting. He'd like the scattered rules collected into a single booklet next year, he loves the tiny polyhedral dice, and he already plans to buy the 2022 edition.

----

Could a five-minute daily dose keep you invested in a story for a whole year, or would you rather binge it in an evening?
